info.title: Academic.page API
info.description:
Read the content of your Academic.page sites, and manage posts, pages, projects, and media.

The content endpoints (`/content/...`) return exactly what each public site shows: published records only, never drafts, scheduled items before their time, deleted records, autosaves, revisions, or private notes. They need a content key and Pro.

The management endpoints (`/sites/{site}/...`) show drafts and accept writes. They need a management key and Pro.

Which sections answer `404 section_not_enabled`: the content endpoints follow the public site, so a section the public site does not show answers it. The management endpoints follow what the admin lets the owner edit for that site type, so they answer it only for a section the site cannot have, such as projects on a course site or lessons on a personal site. A section the admin edits is managed here even while the public site does not show it.

post.description: A file that does not fit is refused with 422 and the same codes as a multipart upload: `upload_too_large` (larger than the plan's per-file limit), `storage_quota_exceeded` (the site's allowance is full), or `bucket_quota_exceeded` (the platform's storage is full). An image the image library cannot read, such as a damaged file, answers 422 `media_processing_failed` and nothing of it is kept. A request without a file answers 422 `validation_failed`; any other failure to store the file, 422 `media_upload_failed`.

post.summary: Start a multipart upload

post.description: The assembled file is checked against the same limits as a single upload: `upload_too_large`, `storage_quota_exceeded`, or `bucket_quota_exceeded`. A file sent as an image (its `content_type` at init) that the image library cannot read, such as a damaged file, answers 422 `media_processing_failed`: the stored parts and anything added to the library are removed, and the site's storage is as it was. Start a new upload to try again. An unknown or expired upload answers 404 `multipart_upload_not_found`.

post.description:
Send a CSL-JSON item as `csl`, simple fields, or both (simple fields win). Publications have no draft state: a new publication is on the public site straight away, so there is no published_at.

The entry is matched against the site first. With `on_match` at `skip` (the default), an entry that matches a publication already there is refused with 409 and the match is named: `publication_exists`, `possible_duplicate`, `preprint_of_existing`, or `ignored_before` (left out of an earlier import). `suggest` brings an entry for a publication already there into it, as an import does: missing details are filled in and differences are offered as a suggestion; it answers 200. `create_anyway` adds a possible duplicate, a preprint, or an ignored entry as its own publication. An entry for a publication already there is never copied.

A DOI is checked against its record in the background; `doi_check.status` says where that stands.

post.description:
Send the BibTeX as a text/plain body, as `bibtex` in a JSON body, or as `file` in a multipart form; a Google Scholar export works as it is. Each entry is checked against the site the way the import page checks it.

`dry_run=true` writes nothing and returns each entry's status: `new`, `existing` (already on the site, with what is new about it), `possible_duplicate`, or `preprint` (of a publication already there), and whether it was left out of an earlier import (`ignored_before`).

A real run imports the entries you `select`, or by default every new and existing entry that was not ignored before. An existing entry is never copied: one with a DOI is checked against its DOI record, and one without is merged field by field, with differences offered as suggestions. DOI checks are queued in one batch.

Only when you send `select` are the entries you left out recorded as ignored, so later imports leave them unselected, as the import page does. An existing entry with nothing new is never recorded. Without `select`, nothing is recorded as ignored.

Needs a write key, even for a dry run.

schema.description: The BibTeX itself. Pass dry_run and select in the query string.

patch.description: Only the fields you send change; a citation field sent as null is removed. The change is written as your own edit, like the publication form. A new or changed DOI is checked against its record, and differences become a suggestion rather than being written.

post.description: Answers 409 with no_pending_suggestion when nothing is waiting, and 409 with edit_conflict for a stale edit_version.

post.summary: Keep the citation and dismiss the suggestion
post.description: This version of the suggestion is not offered again. Answers 409 with no_pending_suggestion when nothing is waiting.

post.summary: The site's public content changed
post.description:
Sent about a minute after the first change a visitor could see: publishing, editing published content, unpublishing, deleting, or changing the profile, menus, or site settings. Changes made in that minute are delivered together. Saving a draft sends nothing. The body does not say what changed: fetch what you need using `content_version`, `updated_since`, or the manifest.

To check a request, split Academic-Page-Signature into `t` and `v1`. Compute the HMAC-SHA256, in lowercase hex, of `t`, a period, and the raw request body, keyed with the webhook's signing secret, and compare it with `v1` in constant time. Reject a request whose `t` is more than five minutes from your clock.

A failed delivery is tried again after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 1 hour, and 3 hours, 5 retries in all, each with the same delivery ID. After the last one the delivery is dropped, and the account page shows that the last delivery failed.

parameters.name: Academic-Page-Event
parameters.description: The event type, the same as `type` in the body.

parameters.name: Academic-Page-Delivery
parameters.description: The delivery ID, the same as `id` in the body. Every retry of one delivery carries the same ID, so you can ignore one you have already handled.

parameters.name: Academic-Page-Signature
parameters.description: `t=<unix time>,v1=<hex>`: the time the request was signed and the HMAC-SHA256 signature.

2XX.description: Received. Any 2xx status within 10 seconds counts as delivered; the body is ignored.

default.description: Any other status, a redirect, a timeout, or no connection counts as a failure and the delivery is retried.

content_structured.description: Advanced: a Tiptap (ProseMirror) document, schema version 1, {"type": "doc", "content": [...]}, for exact control. Most clients send content_markdown instead. Send one of the two, not both.

content_markdown.description: The normal way to set content_structured: Markdown, converted on the server and saved as if the document had been sent. Supported: CommonMark with GFM strikethrough: paragraphs, headings (levels 4 to 6 become 3), bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links (http, https, and mailto only; other links keep only their text), bulleted and numbered lists (nested, with a start number), quotes, fenced and indented code with a language, horizontal rules, and hard line breaks. content_structured.description: Advanced: a Tiptap (ProseMirror) document, schema version 1, {"type": "doc", "content": [...]}, for exact control. Most clients send content_markdown instead. Send one of the two, not both.

content_markdown.description: The normal way to set content_structured: Markdown, converted on the server and saved as if the document had been sent. Supported: CommonMark with GFM strikethrough: paragraphs, headings (levels 4 to 6 become 3), bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links (http, https, and mailto only; other links keep only their text), bulleted and numbered lists (nested, with a start number), quotes, fenced and indented code with a language, horizontal rules, and hard line breaks. Images become links to the image, because a document image must be a file in the site's media library. Tables become one paragraph per row. Raw HTML is kept as plain text, never as HTML. Send content_markdown or content_structured, not both: a request with both is refused with 422 and the code validation_failed.

file_media_id.description: A library file's site media ID to attach: pdf, doc, docx, ppt, pptx, xls, xlsx, txt, csv, html, htm, within the plan's per-file limit. The file moves out of the library into the assignment; the file it replaces is deleted. Null removes the file. Needs file uploads on the plan.

published_at.description: Null keeps or makes it a draft. A time in the past publishes it; in the future, schedules it.

edit_version.description: The edit_version you read. A newer save answers 409 edit_conflict and writes nothing. Leave it out, or send null, to save regardless.

Markdown.description: A rich-text field as Markdown, rendered from the stored document. Null when the record has no document.

MarkdownInput.description: Rich text as Markdown, converted to the editor's document on the server. Supported: CommonMark with GFM strikethrough: paragraphs, headings (levels 4 to 6 become 3), bold, italic, strikethrough, inline code, links (http, https, and mailto only; other links keep only their text), bulleted and numbered lists (nested, with a start number), quotes, fenced and indented code with a language, horizontal rules, and hard line breaks. Images become links to the image, because a document image must be a file in the site's media library. Tables become one paragraph per row. Raw HTML is kept as plain text, never as HTML. Null clears the field.
